introduction: “Be thou a burning moth seeking the light-giving candle.” These passages ask for ardour in teaching the Faith: fire, speed, restlessness, audacity; reading 11 goes so far as to say “cast aside patience and tranquility”. The last readings, from Shoghi Effendi’s time, add that zeal must follow “a clear understanding” of the mission and its methods. Jeremiah’s fire in the bones, the Psalmist’s consuming zeal, Paul’s “woe is unto me, if I preach not”, and the lukewarm church of the Apocalypse are the scriptural kin. Paul also wrote the necessary caution, out of his own past: “a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge”.
questions: What is the difference between the zeal these readings praise and the zeal Paul regretted in himself?
Reading 11 says to cast aside patience; elsewhere the Bahá’í writings prize it. When is each called for?
Reading 8 says enkindlement grows with “mention”. Is fervour a cause of teaching or a result of it?

outside.why: Accept every tribulation; endure taunts. Paul’s account of his own travels: in journeyings often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in weariness and painfulness.
Be a burning moth seeking the candle. Sa‘dí: learn love from the moth, because it burnt, lost its life, and found no voice.
Be a thirsty fish seeking the waters. As the hart panteth after the water brooks.
The steed is ready and the arena wide. So run, that ye may obtain.
He was truly on fire. The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.
Like a blazing furnace, in constant combustion. His word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I could not stay.
The more mention is made, the greater the enkindlement. Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way?
Rise to serve with all their energy. Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.
The opposite condition: because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.
Cast aside patience and tranquillity. Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season.
Many are thirsty and few the cup-bearers. The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few.
“I shall not rest one second as long as life lasts.” Necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!
Write, speak and summon with fervour. We cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.

Zeal after obtaining “a clear understanding of the true character of our mission”. Paul knew zeal without it, his own once: they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. What turns fervour into fanaticism, and what does reading 16 require first?
That the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.
More audacity is needed. Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.
Teaching depends on the individual’s effort. Ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence, and give him no rest.

shortfall: Reading 2, 7, 10 and 14 are personal encouragements without an image of their own.
